Master’s degree from a recognized genetic counseling program or equivalent culmination of education and experience
Minimum three (3) years’ experience in genetic counseling (postmaster’s degree), at least one of which should include administration, supervision, or major responsibilities for independent programs.

The Institute for Precision Health at the University of California, Irvine seeks a motivated and collaborative Genetic Counselor to precision medicine initiatives. This role bridges clinical genomics, data-driven healthcare delivery, and translational research, with the goal of improving appropriate use of genetic testing and advancing personalized care.

The Genetic Counselor will work closely with clinicians, laboratory partners, informatics teams, and researchers to design and administer an institution wide genetic test utilization program that connect to specialty and research programs in genomics and precision health.
Clear and effective communication of complex genetic information to diverse audiences (patients, providers, researchers)
Possess excellent genetic counseling and psychosocial skills to counsel individuals and/or families in a sensitive and confidential manner
Working knowledge of clinical indications for genetic testing across multiple specialties (e.g., neurogenetics, oncology, rare disease)
Proficient in ability to use discretion and maintain all confidentiality
Ability to identify opportunities for quality improvement and innovation in precision health
Written communication skills for documentation, reports, and academic output
Proficient in ability to multi-task with demanding timeframes.
Working knowledge of genetic testing technologies (e.g., gene panels, exome/genome sequencing, CNV analysis, repeat expansion testing)
Ability to work collaboratively as part of a multidisciplinary team
